R10.requirement: clean nominal flight shall produce zero failsafe transitions

reasons: power integrity fault (battery 0.53; diagnosis nominal p=0.98)

attribution.driver: the power_thrust EDGE, not any battery node component
attribution.edge: online.py:546  batt_i - sum(esc_i) - AVIONICS_CURRENT, scale 0.5 A, gate 1.0, joining motor_esc and battery (trust_graph/graph.py:50)
attribution.why_it_recovers: in field mode _lam_upd divides the chi-square by an adaptive running level with tau ~90 s (online.py:433). The edge is grossly inconsistent from the instant the motors draw current, and the alarm clears only because that level rises to absorb it — the layer adapts to the mismatch rather than resolving it.

channel.residual: online.py:575-577  batt_v - (ocv - batt_i*R), ocv = EW(alpha=0.01) of (batt_v + batt_i*R)

first_attribution_was_wrong: The first pass of this script attributed the alarm to the phys_battery voltage residual, on the arithmetic that a 0.002 ohm pack-resistance mismatch at 29 A produces 0.058 V against a 0.06 V scale. The flight data refuted it: components['battery']['phys'] reads 1.000 for the entire flight. In field mode _lam_upd normalises the chi-square by this airframe's own running level and any value below 1.0 maps to consistency exactly 1.0, so that residual never reaches the trust recursion. The resistance mismatch is real and is still reported below, but it is not what fires the alarm. The components are now logged individually rather than assumed.

plant_resistance.caveat: the plant's resting voltage also falls as charge depletes, so this over-attributes late sag to resistance and is an UPPER bound on R_plant over a long flight
plant_resistance.method: R = (v_unloaded_mean - v) / i, per loaded sample; the unloaded mean is the pre-arm resting voltage

question: why does the frozen baseline B1 break R10 on ArduCopter 4.8 when it holds on 3.3 and on the bench?

voltage_channel_secondary_finding.note: real, but NOT the cause of the alarm — see first_attribution_was_wrong

why_phase1_could_not_see_it: ArduCopter 3.3 emits no BATTERY_STATUS and plugins.py:191 reads the battery channel from BATTERY_STATUS only, so the channel was never fresh and online.py:613 gated its availability to zero. The battery node was structurally dead for the whole Phase-I campaign. It cast no phantom healthy vote; the freshness gate handles that correctly. It simply never voted.

The bench simulator generates the battery from csia/sensors/truth.py:143, `batt_v = v_ocv - batt_i * PACK_R_INTERNAL` — the same equation and the same constant the monitor inverts. The residual is identically zero by construction, so no bench test could have detected this.
